Name: Fishing Reborn
Author: xzqute
Description:
[center][size=4][img]https://i.imgur.com/lIyzY2Q.png[/img]
[img]https://img.shields.io/badge/SMAPI-4.5.2+-brightgreen.svg[/img] [img]https://img.shields.io/badge/Stardew%20Valley-1.6.15+-orange.svg[/img] [img]https://img.shields.io/badge/GMCM-Optional-purple.svg[/img]
Pull against the fish's runs, and take a breather before it wears you out.[/size][/center]

[b][size=4]Fishing Reborn[/size][/b][size=4] replaces the fishing bar with a fight in the water. You can watch the fish approach your bait and follow it beneath the surface once it's hooked, with the bobber moving along behind it. Pull against its runs to tire it out, take breaks to recover your grip, and bring it back into the circle for the final pull.[/size]

[size=4]A Catfish makes a second run just as you start to relax after the first. An Eel follows a winding path through the water. Legendary fish have abilities you'll need to work around. You can prepare with groundbait and tackle, but once a fish is on the line, you'll need to watch what it does.[/size]

[size=5][b]1.2.0: Wild Encounters[/b][/size]

[size=4]All 51 ordinary vanilla rod fish now have individual movement patterns, including Goby. Each catch also has a temperament, so two fish of the same species can put up different fights. Some species have special abilities: Octopus spreads ink, Ice Pip leaves floating ice, and Void Salmon creates drifting copies of itself.[/size]

[size=4]Fish can leap out of the water with a timed button prompt. Outdoor fights can also have a whirlpool or a strip of sideways current that carries the fish away. You can turn off ordinary fish abilities or adjust jump challenges in the settings.[/size]

[size=5][b]Fishing in the world[/b][/size]

[size=4]While you wait for a bite, a silhouette swims toward the bait and teases the bobber with shallow dips. It may swim away before biting, leaving you waiting for another fish. Wait for the real bite signal before hooking it: the bobber fully submerges and rises straight back up, with the line following throughout. Reeling in early retrieves an empty bobber without using bait or tackle. During the fight, the fish swims beneath the surface and may leap into the air, with the bobber and line following its movements. Where available, fish use their aquarium sprites and swimming animations.[/size]

[size=4]The approaching silhouette uses the fish selected for that cast. If the preview is unavailable, the silhouette stays hidden and fish selection happens when you hook the catch. Some mods with custom fish-selection rules may need an adapter.[/size]

[size=4]The circle stays where the fight began. Outside it, the risk of escape builds until you pull the fish back. You get a little help pulling inward near the edge. Fish also stay within connected water and turn along the banks when they reach the shore.[/size]

[size=5][b]Learn their habits[/b][/size]

[size=4]Some fish drift quietly before a sudden straight run. Others sweep around you or change sides, and a pause after one burst doesn't always mean they're finished.[/size]

[size=4]All 51 non-legendary vanilla fish caught with a rod have their own movement patterns, including the 19 fish from the standard Fish Tank bundles and Chub from the Field Research Bundle. Catfish run in two directions before resting. Sardines make three small runs, while Eels follow an S-shaped path. Tilapia reverse their arcs, and Sturgeon follow a long straight run with a short sideways escape.[/size]
[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/gjTPLLo.png[/img][/center]

[size=4]Ordinary fish receive one of four temperaments for the catch: Calm, Aggressive, Skittish, or Stubborn. This affects their attack rhythm, recovery, response to pressure, or resistance to fatigue. Some species react to repeated pull directions, frequent releases, or the circle's edge. A few make one last warned run when nearly tired out.[/size]

[size=4]Modded fish without a registered species behavior use five shared movement profiles, with outward runs, sidesteps, and feints between quieter stretches. Nearby banks affect their tactics, and they can respond to low grip or a pull held in the same direction for too long. Custom behavior overrides keep their own rules.[/size]

[td][spoiler][size=4]Glacierfish makes long, straight bursts and rests for a while afterward. During the warning, your pull indicator turns blue; during the burst, it turns at only 25% of its usual speed.

Set your direction before the freeze takes hold. Use the recovery period to turn freely and restore grip before the next run.[/size][/spoiler]

Release the pull button to cool the line. Its long rests after attacks give you time to cool down and recover before the next burst.[/size][/spoiler]

[/table][size=5][b]When to pull[/b][/size]

[size=4]Pulling uses grip, shown by the lightning bolt beside your farmer. Release the button between pulls to recover, and try to save some for the next run. If you use it all, you'll briefly lose the ability to pull. Grip is a temporary reserve for the fight, separate from your farmer's regular energy.[/size]

[size=4]Bubbles show which way the fish will burst. Take a short break, then pull the opposite way as it launches. Get the timing right and you'll land a [/size][b][size=4]counter-pull[/size][/b][size=4], briefly tiring the fish faster while using less grip. Changing direction at the right moment can also trigger it. Counter-pulls help with harder catches, though you can land a fish without them.[/size]

[size=4]Once the fish is tired and inside the circle, an icon and sound tell you it's ready to land. Make the [/size][b][size=4]final pull[/size][/b][size=4] to bring it in. An early attempt makes it resist.[/size]

[b][size=4]Exact timing and bonuses[/size][/b]
[spoiler][size=4]The landing icon appears at 20% fish endurance or below, while the fish is inside the circle.

For a counter-pull, rest for at least 0.15 seconds during the warning, then begin pulling against the burst within its opening window. A timely change of direction also works. The direction tolerance is 45 degrees. The window is 0.65 seconds in Relax, 0.35 in Standard, and 0.2 in Hardcore.

A successful counter grants one second of advantage: correctly opposed pulling tires the fish 50% faster and grip use falls by 25%.[/size][/spoiler]

[size=5][b]Fish jumps[/b][/size]

[size=4]A fish may jump out of the water during a fight. Press the displayed WASD key or controller button before the prompt expires. A held key does not count; release it and press again when prompted.[/size]

[size=4]Success briefly weakens the fish, stops its endurance recovery, and lowers the danger of escape. Failure costs some grip and sends it into an outward escape run. Pull against that run to hold it back.[/size]

[size=4]The fish can land outside the circle, so watch where it comes down. Escape danger pauses in the air, and you get a short response window after an outside landing. Jumps stay over connected water, and most catches have no prompt.[/size]

[b][size=4]Jump timing and settings[/size][/b]
[spoiler][size=4]Each catch can have at most one jump challenge, with none during the first six seconds. The response window is 1.2 seconds in Relax, 0.95 in Standard, and 0.75 in Hardcore.

Success reduces swimming force by 80% for three seconds after landing, pauses endurance recovery, and removes a small amount of remaining endurance. Failure starts a two-second escape run and removes some current grip. These resource changes have fixed caps and cannot empty either bar on their own. An outside landing gives you 0.45 seconds before escape penalties resume.

Jump QTEs are enabled by default. You can disable them or set their frequency from 0.5x to 3x in GMCM or the settings page after the guide. Frequency changes the chance and random wait, while response time and the one-event limit stay the same. Controller buttons assigned to Cancel never appear as prompts.[/size][/spoiler]

[size=5][b]Water currents[/b][/size]

[size=4]An outdoor fight can begin with the circle winding into a whirlpool. The current carries the fish and bobber around the arena, turning the fish's swimming and attack directions with it. Follow the moving warning as you line up a counter-pull.[/size]

[size=4]If there is no whirlpool, a strip of current may cross the circle instead. Small arrows show its direction. It can carry the fish beyond the edge; pull across the strip to get it out of the flow. Whirlpools are more likely in rain, and side currents are more likely in windy weather.[/size]

[b][size=4]Current chances and behavior[/size][/b]
[spoiler][size=4]Outdoor fights have a 10% whirlpool chance in rain and 5% in other weather. The circle forms into a spiral over 2.4 seconds as the current gains strength. At full strength, an unopposed orbit takes about 2.6 seconds. The whirlpool does not pull fish into its center.

Outdoor fights without a whirlpool have a 5% side-current chance, rising to 10% in windy weather. The strip stays in place until the fight ends and carries fish downstream at 1.2 circle radii per second.

Both currents respect shorelines and pause during jumps and mirage relocations. They do not occur in fishing contests.[/size][/spoiler]

[size=5][b]Prepare a fishing spot[/b][/size]

[size=4]Craft some groundbait and select it in your toolbar. Hold the usual Use Tool button to prepare the throw, then release it to send the ball into the water. Crumbs scatter beneath the surface and sway in the water. They thin out as you use the spot, while Glitter Groundbait casts a warm light at night.[/size]

[/table][size=4]Existing saves receive recipes they already qualify for. A failed or cancelled catch does not consume a patch charge. A Challenge Bait multi-catch uses one charge. The patch's effect is chosen when the bobber lands and stays with that cast even if the patch expires during the fight.[/size][/spoiler]

[size=5][b]Worm bait[/b][/size]

[b][size=4][img]https://i.imgur.com/Fr9v3g6.png[/img] Worm bait[/size][/b]

[size=4]You can find worms while tilling fresh soil, with better odds in the rain. Attach them to your rod's normal bait slot.[/size]

[size=4]Worms shorten the wait for bites and sometimes replace an ordinary catch with a fish of higher base value available in that spot. They also improve the chance of a legendary bite when its usual requirements are met.[/size]

[b][size=4]Worm drop rates and bait bonuses[/size][/b]
[spoiler][size=4]Each freshly tilled tile has a 10% chance to drop a worm, rising to 20% if it is raining in that location. After a successful drop, there is a separate 5% chance to receive two worms. An upgraded hoe checks each newly tilled tile; hitting existing tilled soil or watering does not produce worms.

Worm bait reduces the bite wait by a further 25% compared with ordinary bait. On an eligible ordinary catch, it has a 25% chance to select an available fish with a higher base price. If no suitable upgrade exists, the original catch stays. Seasons, weather, time, location, skill requirements, and catch limits still apply.

Legendary bite probability is multiplied by 1.15, a relative 15% increase rather than 15 percentage points. Ordinary fish do not become legendaries through the price upgrade. Legendary catches, the tutorial catch, Fish Ponds, fish frenzies, and flagged special rewards are excluded from that upgrade. Bait consumption follows the game's rules, including Preserving.[/size][/spoiler]

[size=4]Worms still shorten the bite wait and improve the chance of a legendary bite when another mod changes fish selection. Their higher-value replacement is skipped so that mod keeps its chosen catch.[/size]

[size=5][b]Treasure and effect tiles[/b][/size]

[size=4]To collect a chest, steer the tired fish onto its tile and make the final pull there. You'll bring in both together. If the fish runs out of endurance, the chest starts sinking, so plan your approach before the end of the fight.[/size]

[size=4]Temporary effect tiles can appear in the water during a fight. Yellow tiles increase the fish's swimming force; orange tiles reduce it. Steer a difficult fish through an orange tile for some help, and watch out if it's heading toward a yellow one.[/size]

[b][size=4]Effect values[/size][/b]
[spoiler][size=4]Yellow tiles increase swimming force by 30%; orange tiles reduce it by 30%. Both last 2.5 seconds after contact and replace the previous speed effect. They affect the fish's swimming force, not your pull strength.[/size][/spoiler]

[size=5][b]Skill and tackle[/b][/size]

[size=4]Higher Fishing skill gives you more grip for longer pulls. Skill and equipment bonuses that normally increase fishing-bar size expand the circle instead.[/size]

[size=4]Tackle is adapted to the new minigame:[/size]

[table][tr][th][size=4]Tackle[/size][/th]
[th][size=4]Effect in Fishing Reborn[/size][/th]
[/tr]
[tr][td][size=4]Cork Bobber[/size][/td]
[td][size=4]Expands the fishing circle.[/size][/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][size=4]Trap Bobber[/size][/td]
[td][size=4]Slows the risk of escape while the fish is outside it.[/size][/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][size=4]Lead Bobber[/size][/td]
[td][size=4]Smooths changes in your pull.[/size][/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][size=4]Barbed Hook[/size][/td]
[td][size=4]Helps with steering.[/size][/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][size=4]Treasure Hunter[/size][/td]
[td][size=4]Makes the chest's catch area larger.[/size][/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][size=4]Sonar Bobber[/size][/td]
[td][size=4]Reveals the fish's colors beneath the water.[/size][/td]
[/tr]
[/table][size=4]
Auto-Hook still handles the initial hook when a real bite arrives. Challenge Bait also carries over: control mistakes and premature landing attempts can cost you fish from the catch. The game continues to handle catch rewards, XP, quests, quality, and bait consumption, with the groundbait and worm bonuses described above applied where relevant.

[b]Skill bonus[/b][/size]
[spoiler][size=4]Each effective Fishing level adds 5% of the base grip capacity, including food buffs and Master, up to effective level 20. This gives up to 100% additional capacity. Tackle does not multiply this grip bonus. A larger reserve also takes longer to refill completely.[/size][/spoiler]

[size=5][b]Find your own pace[/b][/size]

[size=4]Before your first cast, an illustrated tutorial opens on its first page and walks you from casting to the final pull. It explains grip, countering bursts, the circle, effect tiles, and treasure, then opens a settings page for difficulty, assistance, reduced motion, and jump challenges. You can skip it and return later with fr_guide in the SMAPI console.[/size]

[size=4]There are three difficulty presets:[/size]

[table][tr][th][size=4]Difficulty[/size][/th]
[th][size=4]What to expect[/size][/th]
[/tr]
[tr][td][size=4]Relax[/size][/td]
[td][size=4]Gives you gentler fish, longer warnings, and more time to bring a wandering catch back.[/size][/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][size=4]Standard[/size][/td]
[td][size=4]The default, with time to learn the patterns while keeping an eye on the fish.[/size][/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][size=4]Hardcore[/size][/td]
[td][size=4]Demands quicker responses and more careful use of your grip. Bring developed Fishing skill and strong equipment for the difficult catches.[/size][/td]
[/tr]
[/table][size=4]Automatic pull direction handles steering while you decide when to pull, rest, and land. Toggle pulling lets you press once to start and again to stop. You can also adjust turning speed, inversion, keybinds, and controller dead zone.[/size]

[size=4]Reduced motion, high contrast, fewer decorative effects, sound, and vibration have their own settings. ReducedMotion removes jump height, fish tilt, and moving button prompts while keeping the relocation and result feedback. It also stops continuous whirlpool rotation and animated current highlights. LowEffects reduces fish bending and decorative effects while keeping essential warnings, jump cues, and hazards visible.[/size]

[size=4]Ordinary fish abilities and jump challenges have separate switches. Turning off ordinary abilities keeps species movement and temperaments, and leaves legendary abilities enabled. Jump frequency can be adjusted without changing the time you have to respond.[/size]

[size=4]You can use [/size][b][size=4]Skip[/size][/b][size=4] to land a fish immediately. Skipped catches are capped at silver quality and award neither Perfect nor treasure.[/size]

[size=5][b]Festival fishing[/b][/size]

[size=4]The Ice Festival uses the vanilla fishing minigame. You can still watch a fish approach the bobber, then struggle beneath the ice with the bobber and line following it inside the hole. Skip is available there too, with the same catch limits described above.[/size]

[size=5][b]Installation and settings[/b][/size]
[list=1]
[*][size=4]Use Stardew Valley [b]1.6.15 build 24356[/b] and install [url=https://smapi.io/]SMAPI[/url] [b]4.5.2 or newer[/b].[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Extract the download into [b]Stardew Valley/Mods[/b]. The archive contains the [b]FishingReborn[/b] folder.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Launch through SMAPI and load your save. The tutorial opens before your first cast with the mod enabled. After closing it, cast again to start fishing.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Optional: install [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url] to adjust settings in game. Without it, you can edit config.json; the tutorial also provides the main difficulty and assistance options.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]Settings changes apply to your next catch. When updating, keep a copy of config.json before replacing the mod folder. If you still have the old standalone Fishing Reborn Guide addon, remove it; the tutorial is included in the main mod.[/size]

[size=5][b]Compatibility and feedback[/b][/size]

[size=4]Developed for [b]Stardew Valley 1.6.15 (build 24356)[/b] and [b]SMAPI 4.5.2[/b] on Windows x64. Other game versions fall back to vanilla fishing. Linux and macOS have not been tested.[/size]

[size=4]Custom fish with qualified item IDs use their expected stats and legendary recognition. Long aquarium animations, including SVE's Fiber Goby, are supported. Compatibility with individual fish mods and maps still needs an in-game check. Mods that replace the fishing minigame or automate catches may need adapters.[/size]

[size=4]Fishing Reborn automatically keeps the fishing scene visible with Menu Blur during its custom minigame and Ice Festival fishing, without changing Menu Blur's configuration. If SMAPI reports that the exclusion could not be installed, disable Menu Blur's BlurInFishing option.[/size]

[size=4]Fish Pond catches and unsupported scenarios keep vanilla fishing. A catch that fails during preparation also falls back to vanilla, leaving later attempts available. If an active custom fight fails, reload your save to enable the custom minigame again.[/size]

[size=4]Public API 2.1 supports custom fish behaviors, equipment effects, line modifiers, and appearances. Mod authors can also register independent fish abilities and sprite effects, and respond to fishing events. Existing API 2.0 interfaces remain available.[/size]

[size=4]Fishing sessions stay separate when another split-screen player loads a save or leaves. A two-player split-screen test confirmed that the other player can see the moving bobber and line; the arena, fish, and HUD stay on the angler's screen. A host's active fight also continued when a farmhand left. Separate-machine multiplayer, mixed mod installations, and three- or four-player split-screen still need testing.[/size]

[size=4]A live Fair test covered casting, catching, scoring, and the Star Token reward. A complete timed Ice Festival run and the remaining festival scenarios are still unverified. SVE fish and aquarium data were checked, but full gameplay with SVE or Ridgeside Village has not been verified. The new 1.2.0 behaviors, jumps, and currents have automated checks and visual previews; a complete live gameplay pass is still pending.[/size]

[size=4]For bug reports, include your SMAPI log, mod version, and steps to reproduce. A screenshot or short clip helps with visual or control problems. Feedback on fishing difficulty and fish behavior is also welcome.[/size]
